name: iSH+
subtitle: Turn your iPhone/iPad into a real Linux PC
description:
A Linux terminal that runs a real Linux kernel in a virtual machine (QEMU, with JIT), with the distribution of your choice: Alpine, Debian, Ubuntu, Arch, Fedora and more. x86_64 programs run through FEX. iSH+ enables JIT by itself through LocalDevVPN once it is paired with your device.

Based on iSH. Source: https://github.com/johnnydevelops/ish-plus

versions.localizedDescription:
## Sound

**Linux has sound.** It gets a sound card, and the iPad or iPhone plays it, mixed with other apps' sound.
- **PipeWire and PulseAudio** work as on a computer. They use the card as their ALSA device. For example, `sudo apt install pipewire-audio`, then log out of the desktop and start it again (or restart Linux).
- **When they start:** when your distribution boots with its own init, its systemd user services start them. With iSH+'s own init, the desktop session starts whichever one your distribution has.
- **Who can use it:** your user is in the `audio` group, so programs in any session can use it.
- **Playback only** for now: no microphone.

## JIT shortcut gives your VPN back

The iSH+ JIT shortcut is meant to switch back to the VPN you had on, such as Tailscale, after turning on JIT. That often failed, leaving no VPN connected. It failed in two ways:
- **Shortcuts didn't open:** iSH+ ran the shortcut's last step while it wasn't in front yet, so Shortcuts didn't open.
- **iOS refused the VPN:** iOS rejected connecting your VPN while LocalDevVPN was still on.

iSH+ now waits until it's in front. The shortcut now turns LocalDevVPN off first, waits a second, then connects your VPN.

**Add the shortcut again** (Settings > JIT Setup) to get the new version. On iOS 26 the shortcut still just turns LocalDevVPN off afterwards: iOS 26's Shortcuts can't remember which VPN was on.

## Log out of the desktop with a monitor, keyboard colors

**Log Out of the Desktop with a monitor.** With a monitor connected, or on an iPhone Duo folded, there was no way to end the desktop session. The keyboard's toolbar now has a More button (…) while the desktop shows, with **Log Out of the Desktop**. Linux keeps running, and the monitor shows the terminal again.

**Keyboards follow light and dark mode.** Laptop mode's keyboard and trackpad, and the desktop's extra keys above the iOS keyboard (esc, tab, ctrl…), now use the iOS keyboard's colors: white keys in light mode, dark keys in dark mode. The extra keys looked out of place in light mode before.

**Caps lock shows when it's on.** On laptop mode's keyboard, the caps lock key turns lighter in dark mode or darker in light mode while caps lock is on, and the letters show as capitals. This also works with a hardware keyboard's caps lock. Ctrl, alt and super held for the next key on the desktop's extra keys use the same color.

## Snap applications from the desktop

**Snap applications now run from the desktop.** Starting a snap from the desktop session failed with "User cannot run snap applications on this system". The X11 desktop ran in a background session with its own D-Bus, so snap couldn't reach your user's systemd, which it runs applications through. The desktop is now a regular user session on the display, the way a display manager starts one, and uses your user's D-Bus. Wayland sessions already worked this way.

To get the fix, update, then log out of the desktop and start it again.

## Screens with rounded corners, iOS 26 setup, USB-C security keys

**Terminal on screens with rounded corners** (iPad mini, iPad Air, iPad Pro, iPhones):
- The first line no longer runs into the rounded top corners when the status bar is hidden.
- With the keyboard hidden, there's no longer a gap under the terminal. iPadOS kept reporting an empty keyboard strip at the bottom of the screen, and the terminal used to leave room for it.

**JIT shortcut on iOS 26.** Setup now offers the iSH+ JIT shortcut on iOS 26 too, on the LocalDevVPN page. On iOS 26 it turns LocalDevVPN on while JIT turns on, then off again. On iOS 27 it still switches back to the VPN you had on, such as Tailscale. iOS 26's Shortcuts can't remember which VPN that was.

**Security keys on the USB-C port.** `ssh` with `sk-` keys and other FIDO programs can now use a security key plugged into a USB-C iPad or iPhone. This works with keys that offer FIDO on their smart card interface, such as a YubiKey 5. NFC on iPhone works as before. This is new and hasn't been tested with a key yet: please report how it works for you.

## Desktop fix

**The desktop goes straight into your session again, at your screen's size.** Some desktop packages bring a display manager with them: Debian's and Ubuntu's `xfce4` installs LightDM, for example. Since 1.1.0 starts your distribution's own init system, that display manager started at boot. The Desktop then showed its login screen instead of your session, at a fixed 1280×800 instead of your screen's size.

iSH+ starts desktops itself, so display managers are now kept from starting at boot, under every init system: systemd, OpenRC, runit and sysvinit. One that is already running is stopped when a desktop session starts. They stay installed.

To get the fix on a system that already shows the login screen, update and restart Linux once.

## Turn your iPhone or iPad into a real Linux PC

**Laptop mode.** Connect a monitor (HDMI or AirPlay) and iSH+ shows your terminal session or the Linux desktop on it, at the monitor's full resolution. Your iPad or iPhone becomes the lower half of a laptop:
- a full keyboard with Esc, F1–F12, every symbol, and Control, Alt and Super. Keys combine as on a real keyboard, and a modifier tapped alone applies to the next key.
- a trackpad for the desktop: tap to click, two- or three-finger tap for right or middle click, two-finger scroll, hold then drag.
- Sessions, Settings and Paste buttons. The Sessions menu picks what the monitor shows.

A hardware keyboard or mouse also works. When you disconnect, iSH+ continues with what the monitor showed.

**iPhone Duo.** Half folded, it becomes a mini laptop: the terminal or desktop above the fold, the keyboard and trackpad below.

**Mouse capture.** On iPad, the desktop's new mouse button captures a mouse or trackpad, as in UTM. The pointer no longer stops at the screen's edges, which games need. Control-Option releases it.

**Better pointer.** Trackpad mode now moves Linux's pointer like a real mouse. Touch mode still puts it where you touch. Pointer acceleration is off, because iPadOS already accelerates the motion.

**Wayland and several desktops.** The Sessions menu lists every installed desktop: X11 sessions, window managers, and now Wayland sessions too. These include sway, labwc, Xfce on Wayland and weston, and GNOME and KDE Plasma on Wayland. Pick one to switch to it.

**Distributions boot with their own init system.** systemd, OpenRC (Alpine), runit (Void) and sysvinit (Devuan) now start as on a computer, so services, timers and `systemctl` work. iSH+ runs as one of their services. Extra memory compared with the old init, measured on a Mac: Alpine +8 MB, Devuan +9 MB, Void +22 MB, Debian +45 MB, Ubuntu +59 MB. iSH+'s lighter init is still available: put `ishplus.init=own` in the file `VM/append` in iSH+'s folder.

**Swap.** Linux now has compressed swap in its own RAM (zram, half its size), so under memory pressure idle pages are compressed instead of programs being killed. It's skipped if your distribution sets up its own.

**Fixes:**
- Linux sometimes didn't start at all, with an empty screen. iSH+'s JIT memory could land at an address where the generated code never runs. iSH+ now reserves a safe place for it at launch.
- Firefox, and other programs using the GPU, drew no text with GPU acceleration: a shader instruction was translated wrongly for Apple GPUs.
- `clear` left the terminal scrolled to empty space.
- Servers that only listen inside Linux (such as systemd-resolved's DNS stub) are no longer offered in the menu.

## Faster Linux: 16 KB pages and a new ARM-to-ARM translator

**16 KB memory pages by default.** Linux now runs a 16 KB-page kernel (Debian's prebuilt `linux-image-arm64-16k`), the same page size as iOS, with QEMU's own pages at 16 KB too. Measured on an iPad (9th generation), compared with 4 KB pages:
- starting processes: 26% faster
- copying files with tar: 19% faster
- first run of Python: 14% faster
- first run of gcc: 11% faster
- system calls: 10% faster

The previous 4 KB kernel is still included: **Settings > Linux VM > Memory Pages > 4K Pages**. It's not recommended: it slows down every ARM program, and is only for the rare program that requires 4 KB pages. Your existing distributions boot with either setting.

**New ARM-to-ARM translator.** Most of Linux's instructions now run on the CPU as themselves instead of going through QEMU's general-purpose translator. On the iPad, compared with QEMU's translator:
- system calls: 18% faster
- first run of Python: 32% faster
- first run of gcc: 28% faster

Starting processes is about 4% slower and copying with tar about 5% slower. The interpreter fallback (no JIT) works as before.

**Also:**
- System calls avoid QEMU's global lock on return to programs (about 5% faster even without the translator).
- Instant resume only restores a saved state with the page size it was saved with.

**Known issue:** rarely, Linux doesn't start on the first launch after installing or updating. Quitting and reopening iSH+ fixes it.

Note: this exact build wasn't run on the iPad before release; its changes were each tested on the iPad and on a Mac.

## Fixed

- **Half-precision (FP16) vector math gave wrong results**: the vector instructions `FMLA` and `FMLS` by element on 16-bit floating-point values returned one of their inputs instead of the multiply-add result. Programs using FP16 vector code (some machine-learning, image and audio code) could compute wrong values. Found by new randomized instruction tests that compare the emulator with real ARM hardware.

## Also

- The emulated interrupt controller checks only the interrupts Linux actually uses, so the emulator's timer thread uses less CPU (a little less battery while Linux runs).

Instant resume starts fresh once after updating.

## Faster

Linux in iSH+ is noticeably faster at the things that use the kernel a lot. Measured on an iPad (9th generation), compared with 1.0.3:

| | 1.0.3 | 1.0.4 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Starting programs | 0.78 s | 0.58 s | 26% faster |
| Pipes between programs | 0.26 s | 0.20 s | 24% faster |
| System calls | 0.32 s | 0.26 s | 21% faster |
| Creating files | 0.41 s | 0.37 s | 10% faster |
| apt-cache search | 3.35 s | 3.20 s | 5% faster |

Shell scripts, package installs and anything that starts many small programs benefit most.

What changed in the emulator:
- The kernel's code and memory mappings now stay cached when Linux switches between programs; before, every switch threw them away.
- Entering and leaving the kernel (every system call) skips recomputing the CPU state when nothing changed.
- Every block of emulated code runs 3 fewer instructions, and more unused flag calculations are skipped.

Instant resume starts fresh once after updating.

## Fixed

- **GPU acceleration for your own programs on the Desktop**: the GPU was only usable by root, so programs you ran as your user fell back to slow software OpenGL, and Vulkan-based OpenGL (zink) failed with "failed to choose pdev". It now works for your user, as on a normal Linux system.

Tip: kitty needs OpenGL 3.3. With the Vulkan setting on, it runs with:

    MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE=zink MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=3.3 MESA_GLSL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=330 kitty

Instant resume starts fresh once after updating.

## Fixed

- **iPads and other square screens**: 1.0.1 left an empty strip at the bottom of the terminal and Desktop, because iPadOS reports a bottom safe area even on screens without rounded corners. iSH+ now keeps clear of the screen edges only on screens with rounded corners (iPhones with Face ID, newer iPads).

Instant resume starts fresh once after updating.

## Faster

Linux runs faster, especially system calls, process switches and memory-heavy programs:

- System calls about 30% faster, pipes about 45% faster; Python, apt and compiling a few percent faster.
- Memory copies about twice as fast; matrix and floating-point math 15–20% faster; programs that jump around in memory up to 4× faster.
- QEMU keeps each program's page tables and translated code across process switches, instead of throwing them away.

## Fixed

- **"No route to host" when installing packages** (Void's xbps and others): Linux no longer gets an IPv6 route that iOS can't use, so connections go over IPv4.
- **iPhone screens with rounded corners**: the terminal no longer goes under the home indicator, and the Desktop stays clear of the notch or Dynamic Island and the corners. Square-screen devices are unchanged.
- **iPhone in landscape**: the welcome, JIT and resume screens scroll instead of being cut off.

Instant resume starts fresh once after updating.

iSH+ 1.0: GPU acceleration, more memory for Linux, and a much faster emulator. The emulator changes are large: please report anything that behaves differently from 0.2.3.

## New

- **GPU acceleration** (Settings › Linux VM › Graphics, off by default). Linux's OpenGL runs on the iPad's GPU through VirGL and ANGLE on Metal, and the Desktop Session is drawn on the GPU end to end, with no copies by the CPU. glxgears went from about 25–50 FPS in software to about 285 FPS on an A13 iPad, and the desktop itself is accelerated. Linux pauses its GPU work while iSH+ is in the background.
- **Vulkan** (experimental, with GPU acceleration). Venus gives Linux a Vulkan 1.4 device on the iPad's GPU through MoltenVK, and zink provides OpenGL 3.1 on top of it. On A13 and older GPUs, flat-shaded geometry takes its colour from the first vertex instead of the last.
- **More memory for Linux.** Linux's RAM is held by a helper process, so it no longer counts toward the memory iOS lets iSH+ use (MeloNX's RAM donor technique). Linux can now have up to 60% of the device's RAM, and memory it frees goes back to iOS. On a 3 GB iPad, Linux using 1.4 GB kept iSH+ itself under 500 MB.
- **Pinch to change the text size** in the terminal, as in Termux.

## Faster

On an A13 iPad, compared with 0.2.3:
- **Floating point about 2× faster.** Linux's floating point now runs on the iPad's own FPU, in the generated code, with results and flags identical to real hardware.
- **SHA-1/256/512 and CRC32 on the iPad's own instructions** (about 3× and 8× faster). This speeds up package installs, git, SSH and compression.
- **Faster memory access**, from TLB fills that reuse huge-page mappings, a larger jump cache, and inline lookups for indirect jumps. Byte stores are about 1.5× faster and system calls about 12% faster.
- **Lighter guest kernel settings** for features that only cost time under emulation.

## Fixed

- The Desktop now takes the right size when Linux started it before the Desktop Session was opened.

## Installing

Sideload `iSH-plus-1.0.0.ipa`, or update from the SideStore source; updating keeps your distributions. To try GPU acceleration, turn it on in Settings › Linux VM and restart Linux. Instant resume is off while it is on.

A desktop for Linux, and about 10–15% faster Linux.

## New

- **Desktop Session.** Install an X11 desktop or window manager in Linux (for example `sudo apt install xorg xfce4` on Debian or Ubuntu), and "Desktop Session" appears in the session switcher. It shows Linux's desktop with touch controls like UTM's: tap to click, two-finger tap to right-click, drag the pointer like a trackpad or touch directly, two-finger scroll, pinch to zoom, and a keyboard with Esc, Tab, Ctrl, Alt and arrow keys. Trackpads, mice and hardware keyboards work too. Xfce, MATE, LXQt, LXDE and window managers such as Openbox are found automatically. The desktop is drawn in software for now; graphics acceleration is in progress.
- **SideStore source.** Add `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/johnnydevelops/ish-plus/main/source.json` to SideStore, AltStore or Feather to get new releases as updates.

## Faster

- **About 10–15% faster Linux.** QEMU is now built with full optimization and link-time optimization, which speeds up the lookup it does at every jump in Linux's code. Measured on an iPad: system calls, starting programs, file work, Python and apt are all 10–15% faster.
- **Lighter kernel hardening.** Two kernel hardening features that cost a lot under emulation and add nothing inside iSH+'s sandbox are off: a random stack offset on every system call, and zeroing every kernel allocation.

## Fixed

- **Distributions without a machine ID** now get one at boot, so D-Bus and desktops start.
- **Logging out of the desktop** ends all of its programs.
- **Alert buttons** say "OK" instead of iSH's "k".

## Installing

Sideload `iSH-plus-0.2.3.ipa`, or update from the SideStore source; updating keeps your distributions.

Use your own VPN with iSH+, plus fixes for settings, memory and security keys.

## New

- **The iSH+ JIT shortcut (iOS 27).** If you use another VPN, such as Tailscale, you no longer switch to LocalDevVPN by hand. Add the shortcut in Settings > JIT Setup. When Linux starts, it switches to LocalDevVPN, and once JIT is on it reconnects your VPN, or disconnects LocalDevVPN if none was on. It works like Madeira's JIT shortcut and needs no special entitlement, so it works with free accounts too (#5).
- **Finer memory settings.** The memory slider moves in 16 MB steps.

## Fixed

- **No more freeze in Settings.** Switching Automatic Memory off no longer freezes iSH+ until iOS ends it (#6).
- **Safer automatic memory on large devices.** Automatic memory is at most 60% of the memory iOS lets iSH+ use, and the maximum keeps 10% of it free. On a 12 GB iPhone, Linux got 5.5 GB of a ~6.1 GB limit, and iOS ended iSH+ once Linux used it. It now gets 3.5 GB there. 3 GB iPads keep 1 GB.
- **Security keys: logins one right after another work.** iOS refuses a new NFC session for a moment after the last one closes, so iSH+ now waits for it and retries (#4).

## Installing

Sideload `iSH-plus-0.2.2.ipa`; updating keeps your distributions. See the README for setup, the iSH+ JIT shortcut, and which sideloaders keep which entitlements.

Security key fixes, from testing on an iPhone in #1 and #3.

## Fixed

- **Logins after the first now work.** The NFC session from one login could close the next one, so every login after the first failed instantly. Only one NFC session is now active at a time (#3, by @schmitzoide).
- **The NFC sheet closes once a login is done,** with "Done. You can remove the key.", instead of staying up for 5 seconds.
- **If the key leaves the field mid-login,** iSH+ asks for it again instead of failing.

## Improved

- **One tap less per login.** The key's information is remembered, so a login only needs the key for the signature itself.
- **Clearer failures without NFC.** On an iPad, or on a copy of iSH+ signed without the NFC Tag Reading capability, iSH+ now explains why security keys can't work. Linux also keeps seeing a FIDO2 device instead of `ssh` reporting "device is not fido2".
- **README:** explains which sideloaders and accounts can provide NFC.

## Installing

Sideload `iSH-plus-0.2.1.ipa`. Security keys need a signing profile with the NFC Tag Reading capability: a paid developer account, and a sideloader that applies it. iloader currently doesn't. Updating from 0.2.0 keeps your distributions.

The second preview of iSH+: Linux servers in your browser, instant resume, VM settings, security keys over NFC, and the iSH features that 0.1.0 had lost.

## New

- **Servers open in your browser.** Start a server in Linux and it's at `localhost:<port>` on the device: sessions menu > **Open in Browser**. Servers that only listen on Linux's own localhost (many dev servers) work too. Settings > Linux VM can share the ports with other devices on your network.
- **Instant resume.** When iSH+ goes to the background, Linux is saved, with a checkpoint of its disk so the two match. If iOS closes iSH+, you can resume where you were: iSH+ asks after enabling JIT. With Keep Running in Background on, Linux keeps running and is saved every 10 minutes, since iOS may close iSH+ anyway.
- **Settings > Linux VM**:
  - **Memory:** set automatically for your device (1 GB on 3 GB iPads), or with a slider or a typed value, up to what iOS lets iSH+ use with a margin.
  - **CPU cores.**
  - **Open ports**, and whether they're shared on your network.
- **Bigger disks.** Swipe a distribution in Settings > Distributions > **Disk Size**. Linux grows its file system the next time it starts.
- **Files app.** Files > iSH+ > Shared is `/mnt/ios` in Linux, and `~/iOS` in your home folder.
- **Clipboard.** `pbcopy` and `pbpaste` use the iOS clipboard. tmux and vim can copy to it as well.
- **Shortcuts.** The **Run Command** action runs a command in Linux and returns its output: in the background if Linux is running, otherwise iSH+ opens to start it.
- **Security keys over NFC** (#1, on iPhone). Linux sees a FIDO security key, so `ssh` with `sk-` keys asks you to hold your YubiKey (or another FIDO key) near the iPhone. Not yet tested with a real key: reports are welcome.
- **x86_64 programs built for glibc.** Most prebuilt downloads now work alongside musl ones: FEX uses Ubuntu 24.04's libraries. `apt-x86 install <package>` installs x86_64 Ubuntu packages, replacing `apk-x86`.
- **A new app icon.** iSH's original icon is still available in Settings > App Icon.

## Improved

- **Tailscale and VPN names.** MagicDNS names like `my-mac` resolve in Linux: DNS now goes through iOS's resolver, which follows VPNs' DNS settings.
- **Memory goes back to iOS.** Memory Linux frees is returned to iOS, so iOS is less likely to close iSH+.
- **Ping works for every user,** not only root.
- **New distributions:**
  - Faster first boot: the disk is no longer filled with zeros in the background, which also saves storage.
  - No extra `ubuntu` account in Ubuntu.
- **Terminal:**
  - The history scrolls a row at a time.
  - The margin around the text is back, as in iSH.
  - Caps Lock as Control or Escape works again.
  - The bell flashes the screen.
- **JIT:**
  - StikDebug is the fallback when the built-in enabler isn't set up or fails.
  - The JIT helper exits once JIT is enabled.
- **Smaller app.** The old iSH engine is gone and the QEMU libraries are stripped.

## Fixed

- **Close Session** removes the session and frees its console (#2). The next session on that console starts with a new shell.
- **Disk errors:** no more I/O errors when a new distribution's disk is formatted.

## Installing

Sideload `iSH-plus-0.2.0.ipa` (AltStore, SideStore, Feather...), keeping its entitlements; JIT needs `get-task-allow`. See the README for the setup with LocalDevVPN and pairing. Updating from 0.1.0 keeps your distributions.

Requires iOS 26 or later (iOS 27 to pair on the device). Security keys need an iPhone with NFC.

The first preview of iSH+, a fork of iSH that runs a real Linux kernel in a virtual machine (QEMU, with JIT) instead of iSH's own emulator.

## Highlights

- **Real Linux.** Linux 6.18 runs in QEMU. JIT makes it fast, and iSH+ enables JIT by itself once it is paired with your device. It falls back to StikDebug, or to a much slower mode that runs without JIT.
- **Any distribution.** Install Alpine, Debian, Ubuntu, Arch, Artix, Fedora, openSUSE, Void, Kali, Rocky, Alma and more (arm64), each with its own user account. Add, switch and delete them in Settings > Distributions.
- **x86_64 programs** run through FEX. glibc and musl programs both work, and `apt-x86` installs x86_64 Ubuntu packages.
- **A native terminal** (SwiftTerm) with Liquid Glass, mouse input for terminal apps, Termux-style scrolling and multiple sessions. It keeps running in the background.
- **iOS integration.** The Shared folder in the Files app is `~/iOS` in Linux. `pbcopy` and `pbpaste` use the iOS clipboard, and the Run Command action runs a command from Shortcuts.

## Installing

Sideload `iSH-plus-0.1.0.ipa` with AltStore, SideStore, Feather or a similar tool. Your sideloader re-signs it. Keep its entitlements, since JIT needs `get-task-allow`.

Then:

1. Install and connect **LocalDevVPN**.
2. Pair iSH+ with your device. Use **Pair With This Device** in the setup (iOS 27), or import a pairing file, for example from StikPair.
3. Choose a distribution and create your account. It downloads during setup and installs when it first starts.

## Requirements

- iOS 26 or later. Pairing on the device needs iOS 27.
- Developer Mode on.
- About 100 MB for the app, plus storage for each distribution.

## Known limitations

- The VM has 1 GB of memory.
- Changing distribution requires restarting iSH+.
- A session's history does not survive iSH+ being ended.
- The no-JIT mode is untested.
- Mouse input is untested with a real mouse or trackpad.

privacy.NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription: iSH+ uses your local network to pair with this device, so it can enable JIT by itself.
privacy.NFCReaderUsageDescription: iSH+ uses your security key (YubiKey or another FIDO key) over NFC when programs in Linux, such as ssh, ask for it.
